# The scanner .github/workflows/security.yml installs, pinned, in a file a bot can read.
#
# WHY THE VERSION IS NOT ON THE pip install LINE. A version written into a workflow step is
# watched by nothing at all: Dependabot reads manifests and `uses:` lines, and it does not read
# shell commands. A requirements file is an ecosystem it does read, so a new semgrep release
# arrives here as a pull request instead of ageing in silence. The full account of what that
# silence cost in another of this owner's repositories is in .github/dependabot.yml, above the
# pip entry that watches this file.
#
# WHY IT IS PINNED AT ALL. An analyser that updates itself changes the verdict of a merge gate
# without anybody changing the code, which is the one thing a merge gate must not do. A new
# release turning a green branch red on a commit that touched nothing teaches everybody to
# ignore the check.
#
# THE GATE'S NUMBERS ARE MEASURED WITH THE VERSION BELOW. Measured again on 2026-10-14, when the
# version moved from 1.178.0 to 1.180.0, the newest stable release on the package index that day,
# with the pull request that brought snapshots to the window. That pull request's own Semgrep run,
# on the merge of commit c8ea3cb into main with `--config p/default`: semgrep ran 374 rules over
# 399 files and reported zero findings, and the gate read zero errors at level error and 419 rules.
# The two rule counts are one run read two ways - 374 is semgrep's own summary, 419 the timing
# list in the report, which is what the gate counts. The run on the commit before, d39889d, gave
# the same numbers. Before them the numbers here were from 1.177.0 on 2026-09-22 (131 rules, 301
# files), and 1.178.0 was never measured. Moving this line means measuring again rather than
# assuming the report will look the same.
#
# 399 OF 743 FILES, AND THAT IS NOT A FAULT. Semgrep's own default ignore patterns exclude
# tests/, which is 336 of this repository's files, one picture is skipped for being over 1 MB, and
# the seven other pictures are not among the 399 either - that last part is the arithmetic of the
# count, not a line semgrep prints. So a healthy run of this tree reads src/, site/, .github/,
# packaging/ and the root - about four hundred files - and a collapse to a handful is the shape of
# a scan that ran somewhere else. The gate prints the number on every run for exactly that reason.
#
# Licence, read on 2026-09-22 from that version's own metadata rather than recalled, and read again
# on 2026-10-14 from 1.180.0's, which says the same. The
# package index reports `license_expression` as LGPL-2.1-or-later, with the older `license`
# field null and no licence classifier - which is the modern shape and worth saying, because a
# reader checking the field that used to hold this would find nothing and could conclude the
# licence was unstated. It analyses the source tree in CI and is never linked into anything this
# project ships, so it creates no distribution obligation - see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md for what
# does.
semgrep==1.180.0
